name: pve_mcp_info
title: About this server
description: Says what this server allows, per cluster: read-only or not, elevated changes, guest execution, SSH, sensitive data, dry run, protected guests, which toolsets are loaded and how many tools. Call this first.

name: pve_overview
title: Cluster overview
description: The state of the cluster in one answer: version, quorum, nodes, guest counts, storage usage, HA and recent failed tasks. Whatever could not be read is named in "unavailable". A token only sees what it has audit rights on, so counts may be partial.

task_hours.description: How far back failed tasks count, in hours. Default 24.

name: pve_find_guest
title: Find a guest
description: Finds VMs and containers by vmid, name, tag, status, node, type or IP address, across the cluster. An IP can only be read from a running LXC or from a running VM with its guest agent: those that could not be checked are listed in ip_not_checked, so no match does not mean the address is free.

name.description: Part of the name, in any case.

tag.description: A whole tag, in any case.

node.description: Only guests on this node.

type.description: qemu for VMs, lxc for containers.

ip.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, without prefix length.

include_ips.description: Also read the addresses of each running guest found. One request per guest. Implied by ip.

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_wait_task
title: Wait for a task
description: Waits for a task (UPID) to end and gives its result with the end of its log. A failed task is an error, task_failed. A task that outlasts the wait comes back with still_running: it goes on and is not cancelled.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30).

name: pve_get_task_log_tail
title: End of a task log
description: The status of a task and the last lines of its log, without having to page through it. The log is untrusted text.

lines.description: How many lines, from the end. Default 50.

name: pve_guest_power
title: Start or stop a guest
description: Starts, shuts down, stops or reboots a VM or a container from its vmid, finds the node and the type, and waits for the task. stop cuts the power at once, as pulling the plug would; shutdown asks the guest to stop cleanly. Destructive except for start. A guest that is already in the requested state is left alone.

timeout.description: For shutdown and reboot: seconds the guest has to comply.

force_stop.description: For shutdown: stop the guest hard when it did not comply within the timeout.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30).

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.

name: pve_provision_lxc
title: Provision a container
description: Creates a container from start to finish: free vmid, template found on a storage or downloaded from the appliance index, creation, start, IP address. Each step is reported. If one fails, the error says what was created and what remains: nothing is ever deleted automatically. It never replaces an existing guest. The password is never returned.

template.description: A volume such as local:vztmpl/debian-12-standard_12.7-1_amd64.tar.zst, or a name or start of name such as debian-12-standard, looked up on the storages of the node and then in the appliance index.

node.description: The node. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

vmid.description: The id to use. Default: the next free one.

disk_gb.description: Size of the root disk in GiB. Needs storage.

template_storage.description: Storage to look for the template on and to download it to. Default: the storages of the node that accept templates.

download_template.description: Download the template when it is not on the node. Default true.

net0.description: First network interface, as a Proxmox property string. Default: name=eth0,bridge=vmbr0,ip=dhcp.

ssh_public_keys.description: Public SSH keys for root, one per line.

features.description: Features as a property string, such as nesting=1.

start.description: Start it at the end. Default true.

ip_wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for an IP address after the start. Default 30.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for each task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30). Past this the job stops and reports what remains.

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.

name: pve_provision_vm_from_template
title: Provision a VM from a template

newid.description: The id of the new VM. Default: the next free one.

name: pve_health_check
title: Health check
description: Checks nodes, quorum, storage usage, failed services, failed tasks, HA, Ceph if there is any, replication and subscriptions. Each finding has a severity, the object, the evidence and a suggested action. Sections that could not be read are in "unavailable" and are not counted as healthy: overall says "incomplete" rather than good news. The thresholds used are returned with the answer.

storage_warn_percent.description: Usage from which a storage or root disk is a warning. Default 85.

storage_critical_percent.description: Usage from which it is critical. Default 95.

memory_warn_percent.description: Node memory usage from which it is a warning. Default 90.

task_hours.description: How far back failed tasks count, in hours. Default 24.

name: pve_security_audit
title: Security audit
description: Reads the security-related settings: firewall state (cluster, nodes, guests), privileged containers, API tokens without expiry or privilege separation, second factor on root@pam, powerful ACLs on /, backups, pending updates, certificate expiry. Findings state what the data shows, with evidence and a suggested action. Sections it could not read are named in "unavailable". This is neither a certification nor a statement of compliance, and only sees what this token may read.

cert_warn_days.description: Days before expiry from which a certificate is a finding. Default 30.

include_guests.description: Also read the config and firewall options of each guest. Two requests per guest. Default true.

name: pve_backup_coverage
title: Backup coverage
description: For each guest: whether it is in a backup job, and the age of its last backup found on the backup storages. Also the jobs and the guests that no job covers. A storage or node that could not be read is named in "unavailable", and a guest whose last backup could therefore be missed is listed under not_determined instead of being called unprotected. Having a backup says nothing of whether it restores.

max_age_days.description: A last backup older than this is a finding. Default 7.

These reach the host itself and need PROXMOX_ALLOW_ELEVATED: hookscript, dev[n], mp[n], rootfs, unprivileged. node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

bwlimit.description: Override I/O bandwidth limit (in KiB/s). Default: restore limit from datacenter or storage config. Format: <number> (0 - N).

cmode.description: Console mode. By default, the console command tries to open a connection to one of the available tty devices. By setting cmode to 'console' it tries to attach to /dev/console instead. If you set cmode to 'shell', it simply invokes a shell inside the container (no login). Default: tty.

console.description: Attach a console device (/dev/console) to the container. Default: 1.

cores.description: The number of cores assigned to the container. A container can use all available cores by default. Format: <integer> (1 - 8192).

debug.description: Try to be more verbose. For now this only enables debug log-level on start. Default: 0.

description.description: Description for the Container. Shown in the web-interface CT's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.

dev.description: Device to pass through to the container Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): path=<pve-lxc-dev-string> deny-write=<boolean> gid=<integer> mode=<Octal access mode> uid=<integer> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is dev0 in Proxmox, and dev0 is also accepted as an argument.

entrypoint.description: Command to run as init, optionally with arguments; may start with an absolute path, relative path, or a binary in $PATH. Default: /sbin/init. Pattern: (?^:[^\x00-\x08\x0a-\x1F\x7F]+)

env.description: The container runtime environment as NUL-separated list. Replaces any lxc.environment.runtime entries in the config. Pattern: (?^:(?:\w+=[^\x00-\x08\x0a-\x1F\x7F]*)(?:\0\w+=[^\x00-\x08\x0a-\x1F\x7F]*)*)

features.description: Allow containers access to advanced features. Property string (key=value,...; * required): force_rw_sys=<boolean> fuse=<boolean> keyctl=<boolean> mknod=<boolean> mount=<fstype;fstype;...> nesting=<boolean>

ha-managed.description: Add the CT as a HA resource after it was created. Default: 0.

hookscript.description: Script that will be executed during various steps in the containers lifetime.

hostname.description: Set a host name for the container.

ignore-unpack-errors.description: Ignore errors when extracting the template.

memory.description: Amount of RAM for the container in MB. Default: 512. Format: <integer> (16 - N).

mp.description: Use volume as container mount point. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): volume*=<pve-lxc-mp-string> acl=<boolean> backup=<boolean> idmap=<type:container:disk:range-size[;type:container:disk:range-size;...]> keepattrs=<boolean> mountoptions=<opt[;opt...]> mp*=<pve-lxc-mp-string> quota=<boolean> replicate=<boolean> ro=<boolean> shared=<boolean> size=<disk-size> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is mp0 in Proxmox, and mp0 is also accepted as an argument.

nameserver.description: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if you neither set searchdomain nor nameserver.

net.description: Specifies network interfaces for the container. Property string (key=value,...; * required): bridge=<bridge> firewall=<boolean> gw=<ipv4> gw6=<ipv6> host-managed=<boolean> hwaddr=<mac-addr> ip=<pve-ipv4-config> ip6=<pve-ipv6-config> link_down=<boolean> mtu=<integer> name*=<string> rate=<mbps> tag=<integer> trunks=<vlanid[;vlanid...]> type=<veth> Numbered items, such as {"0": "virtio,bridge=vmbr0"}: key 0 is net0 in Proxmox, and net0 is also accepted as an argument.

onboot.description: Specifies whether a container will be started during system bootup. Default: 0.

ostemplate.description: The OS template or backup file.

ostype.description: OS type. This is used to setup configuration inside the container, and corresponds to lxc setup scripts in /usr/share/lxc/config/<ostype>.common.conf. Value 'unmanaged' can be used to skip and OS specific setup.

pool.description: Add the VM to the specified pool.

protection.description: Sets the protection flag of the container. This will prevent the CT or CT's disk remove/update operation. Default: 0.

rootfs.description: Use volume as container root. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): volume*=<pve-lxc-mp-string> acl=<boolean> idmap=<type:container:disk:range-size[;type:container:disk:range-size;...]> mountoptions=<opt[;opt...]> quota=<boolean> replicate=<boolean> ro=<boolean> shared=<boolean> size=<disk-size>

node.description: The cluster node name. Optional: found from the vmid when left out.

affinity.description: List of host cores used to execute guest processes, for example: 0,5,8-11

agent.description: Enable/disable communication with the QEMU Guest Agent and its properties. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): enabled*=<boolean> freeze-fs=<boolean> fstrim_cloned_disks=<boolean> type=<virtio|isa>

allow-ksm.description: Allow memory pages of this guest to be merged via KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging). Default: 1.

arch.description: Virtual processor architecture. Defaults to the host architecture.

audio0.description: Configure a audio device, useful in combination with QXL/Spice. Property string (key=value,...; * required): device*=<ich9-intel-hda|intel-hda|AC97> driver=<spice|none>

autostart.description: Automatic restart after crash (currently ignored). Default: 0.

balloon.description: Amount of target RAM for the VM in MiB. The balloon driver is enabled by default, unless it is explicitly disabled by setting the value to zero. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

boot.description: Specify guest boot order. Use the 'order=' sub-property as usage with no key or 'legacy=' is deprecated. Format: [[legacy=]<[acdn]{1,4}>] [,order=<device[;device...]>].

bootdisk.description: Enable booting from specified disk. Deprecated: Use 'boot: order=foo;bar' instead. Pattern: (ide|sata|scsi|virtio)\d+

cdrom.description: This is an alias for option -ide2 Format: <volume>.

cicustom.description: cloud-init: Specify custom files to replace the automatically generated ones at start. Format: [meta=<volume>] [,network=<volume>] [,user=<volume>] [,vendor=<volume>].

cipassword.description: cloud-init: Password to assign the user. Using this is generally not recommended. Use ssh keys instead. Also note that older cloud-init versions do not support hashed passwords.

citype.description: Specifies the cloud-init configuration format. The default depends on the configured operating system type (`ostype`. We use the `nocloud` format for Linux, and `configdrive2` for windows.

ciupgrade.description: cloud-init: do an automatic package upgrade after the first boot. Default: 1.

ciuser.description: cloud-init: User name to change ssh keys and password for instead of the image's configured default user.

cores.description: The number of cores per socket. Default: 1. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

cpulimit.description: Limit of CPU usage. Default: 0. Format: <number> (0 - 128).

cpuunits.description: CPU weight for a VM, will be clamped to [1, 10000] in cgroup v2. Default: cgroup v1: 1024, cgroup v2: 100. Format: <integer> (1 - 262144).

delete.description: A list of settings you want to delete.

description.description: Description for the VM. Shown in the web-interface VM's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.

digest.description: Prevent changes if current configuration file has different SHA1 digest. This can be used to prevent concurrent modifications.

name: pve_run_backup
title: Run backup
description: Create backup. [POST /nodes/{node}/vzdump. Needs: The user needs 'VM.Backup' permissions on any VM, and 'Datastore.AllocateSpace' on the backup storage (and fleecing storage when fleecing is used). The 'tmpdir', 'dumpdir', 'script' and 'job-id' parameters are restricted .... Requires root@pam. Destructive with some argument values. These reach the host itself and need PROXMOX_ALLOW_ELEVATED: script, dumpdir, tmpdir.]

node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

all.description: Backup all known guest systems on this host. Default: 0.

bwlimit.description: Limit I/O bandwidth (in KiB/s). Default: 0. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

dumpdir.description: Store resulting files to specified directory.

exclude-path.description: Exclude certain files/directories (shell globs). Paths starting with '/' are anchored to the container's root, other paths match relative to each subdirectory.

fleecing.description: Options for backup fleecing (VM only). Format: [[enabled=]<1|0>] [,storage=<storage ID>].

ionice.description: Set IO priority when using the BFQ scheduler. For snapshot and suspend mode backups of VMs, this only affects the compressor. A value of 8 means the idle priority is used, otherwise the best-effort priority is used with the specified value. Default: 7. Format: <integer> (0 - 8).

job-id.description: The ID of the backup job. If set, the 'backup-job' metadata field of the backup notification will be set to this value. Only root@pam can set this parameter. Pattern: \S+

lockwait.description: Maximal time to wait for the global lock (minutes). Default: 180. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

mailnotification.description: Deprecated: use notification targets/matchers instead. Specify when to send a notification mail Default: always.

mailto.description: Deprecated: Use notification targets/matchers instead. Comma-separated list of email addresses or users that should receive email notifications.

notes-template.description: Template string for generating notes for the backup(s). It can contain variables which will be replaced by their values. Currently supported are {{cluster}}, {{guestname}}, {{node}}, and {{vmid}}, but more might be added in the future. Needs to be a single line, newline and backslash need to be escaped as '\n' and '\\' respectively. Needs storage.

notification-mode.description: Determine which notification system to use. If set to 'legacy-sendmail', vzdump will consider the mailto/mailnotification parameters and send emails to the specified address(es) via the 'sendmail' command. If set to 'notification-system', a notification will be sent via PVE's notification system, and the mailto and mailnotification will be ignored. ... Default: auto.

pbs-change-detection-mode.description: PBS mode used to detect file changes and switch encoding format for container backups.

pigz.description: Use pigz instead of gzip when N>0. N=1 uses half of cores, N>1 uses N as thread count. Default: 0.

pool.description: Backup all known guest systems included in the specified pool.

protected.description: If true, mark backup(s) as protected. Needs storage.

prune-backups.description: Use these retention options instead of those from the storage configuration. Default: keep-all=1.

remove.description: Prune older backups according to 'prune-backups'. Default: 1.

stdexcludes.description: Exclude temporary files and logs. Default: 1.

stdout.description: Write tar to stdout, not to a file.

stop.description: Stop running backup jobs on this host. Default: 0.

stopwait.description: Maximal time to wait until a guest system is stopped (minutes). Default: 10. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

storage.description: Store resulting file to this storage. Format: <storage ID>.

tmpdir.description: Store temporary files to specified directory.

vmid.description: The ID of the guest system you want to backup.

zstd.description: Zstd threads. N=0 uses half of the available cores, if N is set to a value bigger than 0, N is used as thread count. Default: 1.

wait.description: If the call starts a task, wait for its end (default true). A failed task is reported as an error.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30). Past this it keeps running: see pve_wait_task.

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.

name: pve_api_search
title: Search the Proxmox API
description: Searches the catalog of 680 Proxmox API methods: path, description and parameter names. Each result gives the tool that calls it, and the gate this server applies. Every method has its own tool, but tool lists are filtered by PROXMOX_TOOLSETS and by what the instance allows: a result whose tool is not in your list can still be called with pve_api_read or pve_api_write, under the same policy.

query.description: Words that must all appear, such as "lxc snapshot" or "firewall ipset".

page_limit.description: Results per page (default 30).

page_offset.description: Results to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_api_describe
title: Describe an API method
description: Gives everything known about one API method: all parameters with types and allowed values, privileges needed, what it returns, the gate this server applies and the tool that calls it. Use this before a call that failed validation, or to build a property string such as net0.

path.description: The template (/nodes/{node}/qemu), or a concrete path (/nodes/pve1/qemu).

name: pve_api_read
title: Read any API path
description: Calls any GET method by path, under the same policy as the dedicated tools: gate read, or sensitive when that is allowed. For what is not in your tool list. A path that is not in the catalog counts as sensitive. Secrets are redacted.

path.description: API path, without /api2/json, such as /nodes/pve1/qemu/100/config. It may also be a template with {placeholders}, filled from path_params.

path_params.description: Values for {placeholders} in the path. The way to pass a value holding a slash, such as a volume id: path /nodes/pve1/storage/local/content/{volume}, path_params {"volume": "local:iso/x.iso"}.

params.description: Parameters. Booleans become 1/0, arrays repeat the key, and {"0": "..."} under net becomes net0.

page_limit.description: Rows per page, when the answer is a list.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_api_write
title: Write to any API path
description: Calls any POST, PUT or DELETE method by path, for what is not in your tool list. The same policy applies: the gate of the method is checked, including elevated, guest_exec and console, and blocked endpoints stay blocked. A path that is not in the catalog counts as elevated. A task id in the answer is waited for. Prefer a dedicated tool whenever one exists.

path.description: API path, without /api2/json, such as /nodes/pve1/qemu/100/config. It may also be a template with {placeholders}, filled from path_params.

params.description: Parameters. Booleans become 1/0, arrays repeat the key, and {"0": "..."} under net becomes net0.

wait.description: If the call starts a task, wait for its end (default true).

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30).
